docs.purpose: Opens one saved job from the user's board, or straight from a push notification. It shows the address, permit number, status badges for delayed and urgent jobs, and an animated timeline bar showing the predicted start date with best-case and worst-case dates either side. Opening the screen also marks the job as seen, which quiets the amber update flash back on the board.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through 2 contracts: `/api/leads/flight-board`, `/api/leads/flight-board/detail/[id]`. Behind those contracts, the data comes from `entitlements`, `lead_views`, `permits`, `trade_forecasts` and `user_profiles`. It also holds client-side state in `flightBoardSeenStore`, which is the part a server-driven projection has to absorb or justify.
docs.under_126: **REBUILD** — it holds Layer-3 state (`flightBoardSeenStore`), so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the DETAIL renderer (one entity, a single-param query key, declared sections), reading by reference: `/api/leads/flight-board`, `/api/leads/flight-board/detail/[id]`. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

identity.owner: unassigned (no CODEOWNERS file and no owner registry exists in the repo — measured 2026-09-15)

versioning.why: The cold-boot fallback parses the same FlightBoardDetail shape the list item satisfies, so the two payloads must stay structurally compatible; adding a field is safe, removing one breaks both readers.

inputs.why: It first tries to find the permit inside the already-cached ["flight-board"] result and only calls GET /api/leads/flight-board/detail/:id when the board resolved without a hit — a push-notification cold-boot path.

outputs.why: Opening the screen writes the permit's updated_at into the MMKV last-seen map so the parent board stops flashing amber; no contract is called and no server row changes.
outputs.rollback: none — markSeen is a monotonic local write with no server counterpart to roll back.

state.why: Its only owned state is the flightBoardSeenStore entry it writes on mount; the forecast gauge uses Reanimated shared values, which are Layer-5 UI-only.

staleness.why: The cache-hit path reuses the board's 30-second entry; the cold-boot fallback query declares its own 60-second staleTime.

session.why: The route is under `/api/leads`; the hook additionally refuses to fire until authStore holds an accessToken so a cold-boot deep link cannot 401.

rls_class.why: The detail row is one of the user's own lead_views rows joined to permits/trade_forecasts; lead_views carries the auth.uid() owner policies.

guards.rate_bucket: none — the flight-board detail route calls no withRateLimit

checks.why: mobile/__tests__/useFlightJobDetail.test.ts pins the detail payload and the retry guard that must not burn retries on deterministic 404s.
The key is the single-param ["flight-job-detail", id] the DETAIL archetype requires — one scalar, no object literal.

Both the board query and the fallback resolving without a hit render "Job not found in board." ([flight-job].tsx:213-215); a skeleton covers the in-flight window so the push deep link never flashes not-found.
The markSeen write is what quietens the parent board's amber flash; flightBoardSeenStore.test.ts locks the comparison rule this write feeds.

errors.why: There is no error branch at all — a failed fallback fetch and a genuine 404 collapse into the same inline "Job not found in board." message.

classes.ui: Inline "Job not found in board." — a server failure is indistinguishable from a miss on this screen.
FlightJobDetailSchemaError: not retried, rendered as the same inline "Job not found in board.".

emits.why: flight_job_detail_viewed fires once per resolved permit (deps gated on permit_num/revision_num) and is NOT DEV-gated, unlike its parent board screen.

offers.why: No sponsored placement is rendered: the only slot component in the Expo tree is SponsorSlot, and it returns null unless EXPO_PUBLIC_PARCEL_SPONSORS=1.

metering.why: Nothing here is counted: the Spec 126 §7 usage ledger table does not exist (grep for usage_events in the introspected drizzle schema returns 0 hits), and the only quota-shaped counter, user_profiles.lead_views_count, is incremented solely by POST /api/leads/view, which has no mobile caller.

config.why: The surface consumes no registered logic variable: the only server-side tunable in this path, user_profiles.radius_cap_km, is a per-user admin column, not a logic_variables row.

sharing.why: Its primary read is the flight board's own cache entry; only the cold-boot /detail/:id route is exclusive to this surface.

limitations.what: A failed fetch is rendered as "Job not found in board." — an error is presented to the user as a miss.
limitations.measured: [flight-job].tsx:209-215 has one non-loading fallback branch keyed on `!item`; detailQuery.isError is never read.

limitations.what: The p25/p75 gauge springs open on every mount regardless of the OS reduce-motion setting.
limitations.measured: [flight-job].tsx:69-76 calls withSpring unconditionally; no AccessibilityInfo check exists in mobile/.
limitations.check_id: none — checks[].kind has no reduced-motion value; raised as a vocabulary escalation per Spec 128 §4

limitations.what: The screen's dominant failure — HTTP 404 from GET /api/leads/flight-board/detail/:id — cannot be declared: errors.classes has no 404 value.
limitations.measured: surface.schema.json errors.classes enum = 400/401/403/429/500/schema_drift/offline (checked 2026-09-15); the route returns 404 for a permit not on the user's board.

notes: The screen defends against an inverted server forecast (p75 < p25) by swapping the bounds so the bar width is never negative ([flight-job].tsx:52-58) — a client-side guard compensating for a server-side invariant nobody asserts in SQL.

programme.why: Flight center — the other product. Fenced from the parcel tool by Spec 128 R-03; inventoried only.
